body.text:
oṃ devā ha vai svargalokam āyaṃs te rudram apṛcchan ko bhavān iti /
so 'bravīd aham ekaḥ prathamam āsodvartāmi ca bhaviṣyāmi ca nānyaḥ kaścin matto vyatirikta iti /
so 'ntarād antaraṃ prāviśat diśaś cāntaraṃ prāviśat so 'haṃ nityānityo vyaktāvyakto brahmā brahmāhaṃ prāñcaḥ pratyañco 'haṃ dakṣiṇāṃ ca udañco 'ham adhaś cordhvaś cāhaṃ diśaś ca pratidiśaś cāhaṃ pumān apumān striyaś cāhaṃ sāvitry ahaṃ gāyatry ahaṃ triṣṭubjagatyanuṣṭup cāhaṃ chando 'haṃ satyo 'haṃ gārhapatyo dakṣiṇāgnir āhavanīyo 'haṃ gaur ahaṃ gaury aham ṛg ahaṃ yajur ahaṃ sāmāham atharvāṅgiraso 'haṃ jyeṣṭho 'haṃ śreṣṭho'haṃ variṣṭho 'ham āpo 'haṃ tejo 'haṃ guhyo 'ham araṇyo 'ham akṣaram ahaṃ kṣaram ahaṃ puṣkaram ahaṃ pavitram aham ugraṃ ca baliś ca purastāj jyotir ity aham eva sarvebhyo mām eva sa sarvaḥ samāyo māṃ veda sa devān veda sarvāṃś ca vedān sāṅgān api brahma brāhmaṇaiś ca gāṃ gobhir brāhmaṇān brāhmaṇyena havir haviṣā āyur āyuṣā satyena satyaṃ dharmeṇa dharmaṃ tarpayāmi svena tejasā /
tato ha vai te devā rudram apṛcchan te devā rudram apaśyan te devā rudram adhyāyan te devā ūrdhvabāhavo rudraṃ stuvanti //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. The gods went to the heavenly world and asked <s>Rudra</s>: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I alone was first; I am [now] and I shall be; there is no other whatsoever apart from me.' He entered the interior from the interior, and entered the interior of the directions. 'I am the eternal and the non-eternal, the manifest and the unmanifest. I am <s>Brahmā</s>, I am <s>Brahman</s>. I am the east and the west, I am the south and the north, I am below and above, I am the directions and the intermediate directions. I am male, non-male, and female. I am <s>Sāvitrī</s>, I am <s>Gāyatrī</s>, I am <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, <s>Jagatī</s>, and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. I am meter. I am truth. I am the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire], the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>, and the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire]. I am the bull, I am the cow. I am the <s>Ṛg</s> [Veda], I am the <s>Yajur</s> [Veda], I am the <s>Sāma</s> [Veda], I am the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s>. I am the eldest, I am the best, I am the greatest. I am the waters, I am radiance. I am the hidden one, I am the forest-dweller. I am the imperishable, I am the perishable. I am the lotus, I am the purifier. I am fierce and powerful. Before all, light — that am I. From all, unto me alone — he who is the totality converges in me. He who knows me knows the gods, all the <s>Vedas</s> with their limbs, <s>Brahman</s> through <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, cows through cows, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> through <s>brāhmaṇya</s> (Brahminhood), oblation through oblation, life through life, truth through truth, <s>dharma</s> through <s>dharma</s> — I satisfy [all] with my own radiance.' Then the gods asked <s>Rudra</s>; the gods beheld <s>Rudra</s>; the gods studied <s>Rudra</s>; the gods, with arms raised, praise <s>Rudra</s>.

body.text: oṃ yo vai rudraḥ sa bhagavān yaś ca brahmā tasmai vai namonamaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. He who is <s>Rudra</s>, He is the Blessed One; and He who is <s>Brahmā</s> — to Him, repeated homage.

body.text: yo vai rudraḥ sa bhagavān yaś ca viṣṇus tasmai vai namonamaḥ //
body.translated_text: He who is <s>Rudra</s>, He is the Blessed One; and He who is <s>Viṣṇu</s> — to Him, repeated homage.

body.text:
yo vai rudraḥ sa bhagavān yā ca pṛthivī tasmai vai namonamaḥ /
yo vai rudraḥ sa bhagavān yac cāntarikṣaṃ tasmai vai namonamaḥ //
body.translated_text: He who is <s>Rudra</s>, He is the Blessed One; and that which is the earth — to Him, repeated homage. He who is <s>Rudra</s>, He is the Blessed One; and that which is the atmosphere (<s>antarikṣa</s>) — to Him, repeated homage.

body.translated_text: He who is <s>Rudra</s>, He is the Blessed Lord, and that which is Truth — to Him, salutations again and again!

body.text: yo vai rudraḥ sa bhagavān yac ca sarvaṃ tasmai vai namonamaḥ //
body.translated_text: He who is <s>Rudra</s>, He is the Blessed Lord, and that which is the All — to Him, salutations again and again!

body.text:
bhas te ādir madhyaṃ bhuvas te svas te śīrṣaṃ viśvarūpo 'si brahmaikas tvaṃ dvidhā tridhā vṛddhis tvaṃ śāntis tvaṃ puṣṭis tvaṃ hutam ahutaṃ dattam adattaṃ sarvam asarvaṃ viśvam aviśvaṃ kṛtam akṛtaṃ param aparaṃ parāyaṇaṃ ca tvam /
apām asomam amṛtā abhūm āgan me jyotir avidāma devān /
kiṃ nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ /
kim u dhūrtir amṛtaṃ martyasya somasūryapurastāt sūkṣmaḥ puruṣaḥ /
sarvaṃ jagaddhitaṃ vā etad akṣaraṃ prājāpatyaṃ saumyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ puruṣaṃ grāhyam aguhyena bhāvaṃ bhāvena saumyaṃ saumyena sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmena vāyavyaṃ vāyavyena grasati tasmai mahāgrāsāya vai namonamaḥ /
hṛdisthā devatāḥ sarvā hṛdi prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
hṛdi tvam asi yo nityaṃ tisro mātrāḥ paras tu saḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bhas</s> is Your beginning, <s>Bhuvas</s> Your middle, <s>Svas</s> Your head. You are of universal form. You are the one <s>Brahman</s> (Absolute Reality) — twofold, threefold. You are growth, You are peace, You are nourishment. What is offered and what is not offered, what is given and what is not given, all and non-all, universe and non-universe, created and uncreated, the supreme and the non-supreme, and the ultimate refuge — all this are You. / "We have drunk the <s>Soma</s>, we have become immortal, we have reached the light, we have found the gods. What now can hostility do to us? What indeed can the treachery of a mortal do to the immortal?" / Before <s>Soma</s> and <s>Sūrya</s> stands the subtle <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person). This imperishable, <s>Prājāpatya</s> (belonging to Prajāpati), gentle, subtle <s>Puruṣa</s>, beneficial to all the world, is to be grasped — by the non-hidden one grasps existence, by existence the gentle, by the gentle the subtle, by the subtle the airy, and by the airy He devours all. To that Great Devourer, salutations again and again! / All deities abide in the heart; all vital breaths are established in the heart. You are in the heart — He who is eternal. The three <s>mātrās</s> (measures of Oṃ), and beyond them is He.

body.text: tasyottarataḥ śirodakṣiṇataḥ pādau ya uttarataḥ sa oṃkāraḥ ya oṃkāraḥ sa praṇavaḥ yaḥ praṇavaḥ sa sarvavyāpī yaḥ sarvavyāpī so 'nantaḥ yo 'nantas tat tāraṃ yat tāraṃ tac chuklaṃ yac chuklaṃ tat sūkṣmaṃ yat sūkṣmaṃ tad vaidyutaṃ yad vaidyutaṃ tat paraṃ brahma yat paraṃ brahma sa ekaḥ yaḥ ekaḥ sa rudraḥ yo rudraḥ sa īśānaḥ ya īśānaḥ sa bhagavān maheśvaraḥ //
body.translated_text: His head is to the north, His feet to the south. That which is to the north is <s>Oṃkāra</s>. That which is <s>Oṃkāra</s> is <s>Praṇava</s> (the sacred syllable Oṃ). That which is <s>Praṇava</s> is all-pervading. That which is all-pervading is infinite. That which is infinite is <s>Tāra</s> (the saving syllable). That which is <s>Tāra</s> is luminous. That which is luminous is subtle. That which is subtle is lightning-like. That which is lightning-like is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. That which is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> is the One. That which is the One is <s>Rudra</s>. That which is <s>Rudra</s> is <s>Īśāna</s> (the Supreme Ruler). That which is <s>Īśāna</s> is the Blessed Lord <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord).

body.text:
atha kasmād ucyate oṃkāraḥ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva prāṇān ūrdhvam utkrāmayati tasmād ucyate oṃkāraḥ /
atha kasmād ucyate praṇavaḥ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvāṅgirasaṃ brahma brāhmaṇebhyaḥ praṇāmayati nāmayati ca tasmād ucyate praṇavaḥ /
atha kasmād ucyate sarvavyāpī yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva yathā snehena palalapiṇḍam iva śāntarūpam otaprotam anuprāpto vyatiṣaktaś ca tasmād ucyate sarvavyāpī /
atha kasmād ucyate 'nantaḥ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva tiryag ūrdhvam adhastāc cāsyānto nopalabhyate tasmād ucyate 'nantaḥ /
atha kasmād ucyate tāraṃ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva garbhajanmavyādhijarāmaraṇasaṃsāramahābhayāt tārayati trāyate ca tasmād ucyate tāram /
atha kasmād ucyate śuklaṃ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva klandate klāmayati ca tasmād ucyate śuklam /
atha kasmād ucyate sūkṣmaṃ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva sūkṣmo bhūtvā śarīrāṇy adhitiṣṭhati sarvāṇi cāṅgāny abhimṛśati tasmād ucyate sūkṣmam /
atha kasmād ucyate vaidyutaṃ yasmād uccāryamāṇa eva vyakte mahati tamasi dyotayati tasmād ucyate vaidyutam /
atha kasmād ucyate paraṃ brahma yasmāt param aparaṃ parāyaṇaṃ ca bṛhad bṛhatyā bṛṃhayati tasmād ucyate paraṃ brahma /
atha kasmād ucyate ekaḥ yaḥ sarvān prāṇān saṃbhakṣya saṃbhakṣaṇenājaḥ saṃsṛjati visṛjati tīrtham eke vrajanti tīrtham eke dakṣiṇāḥ pratyañca udañcaḥ prāñco 'bhivrajanty eke teṣāṃ sarveṣām iha saṃgatiḥ /
sākaṃ sa eko bhūtaś carati prajānāṃ tasmād ucyate ekaḥ /
atha kasmād ucyate rudraḥ yasmād ṛṣibhir nānyair bhaktair drutam asya rūpam upalabhyate tasmād ucyate rudraḥ /
atha kasmād ucyate īśānaḥ yaḥ sarvān devān īśate īśānībhir jananībhiś ca śaktibhiḥ /
abhittvā śūraṇo numo dugdhā iva dhenavaḥ /
īśānam asya jagataḥ svadarśam īśānam indratasthuṣa iti tasmād ucyate īśānaḥ /
atha kasmād ucyate bhagavān maheśvaraḥ yasmād bhaktājñānena bhajaty anugṛhṇāti ca vācaṃ saṃsṛjati visṛjati ca sarvān bhāvān parityajyātmajñānena yogaiśvaryeṇa mahati mahīyate tasmād ucyate bhagavān maheśvaraḥ tad etad rudracaritam //

eko ha devaḥ pradiśo 'nu sarvāḥ pūrvo ha jātaḥ sa u garbha antaḥ /
sa eva jātaḥ sa janiṣyamāṇaḥ pratyaṅjanās tiṣṭhati sarvatomukhaḥ /
eko rudro na dvitīyāya tasmai ya imāṃl lokān īśata īśānībhiḥ /
pratyaṅjanās tiṣṭhati saṃcukocāntakāle saṃsṛjya viśvā bhuvanāni goptā /
yo yoniṃ yonim adhitiṣṭhaty eko yenedaṃ sarvaṃ vicarati sarvam /
tam īśānaṃ varadaṃ devam īḍyaṃ nicāyyemāṃ śāntim atyantam eti /
kṣamāṃ hitvā hetujālasya mūlaṃ buddhyā saṃcitaṃ sthāpayitvā tu rudro rudram ekatvam āhuḥ /
śāśvataṃ vai purāṇam iṣam ūrjeṇa paśavo 'nunāmayantaṃ mṛtyupāśān /
tad etenātmann etenārdhacaturthena mātreṇa śāntiṃ saṃsṛjati paśupāśavimokṣaṇam yā sā prathamā mātrā brahmadevatyā raktā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacched brahmapadam /
yā sā dvitīyā mātrā viṣṇudevatyā kṛṣṇā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacched vaiṣṇavaṃ padam /
yā sā tṛtīyā mātrā īśānadevatyā kapilā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacched aiśānaṃ padam /
yā sārdhacaturthī mātrā sarvadevatyāvyaktībhūtā khaṃ vicarati śuddhā sphaṭikasaṃnibhā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacchet padam anāmayam /
tad etad upāsīta munayo vāgvadanti na tasya grahaṇam ayaṃ panthā vihita uttareṇa yena devā yānti yena pitaro yena ṛṣayaḥ param aparaṃ parāyaṇaṃ ceti //
body.translated_text: The One God (<s>Deva</s>) who pervades all directions, born first, He who is within the womb — He who has been born, He who is to be born — facing beings, He stands with faces everywhere. One is <s>Rudra</s>; there is no second to Him, who rules these worlds with His sovereign powers. Facing beings He stands, and at the end of time, having created all worlds, He withdraws [them], the Protector. He who alone presides over every womb, by whom all this moves about entirely — having recognized that Lord (<s>Īśāna</s>), the Boon-Giver, the praiseworthy God, one attains peace eternal. Having abandoned forbearance, the root of the net of causes, having established [all] through intellect in <s>Rudra</s> — they declare <s>Rudra</s> to be the One. The eternal, the ancient, with food and vigor, He causes beings to overcome the snares of death. By this self, by this three-and-a-half <s>mātrā</s> (measure [of Oṃ]), He creates peace — the liberation from the bonds of the bound soul (<s>paśupāśavimokṣaṇa</s>). That which is the first <s>mātrā</s>, having <s>Brahmā</s> as its deity, red in color — whoever meditates on it constantly, he attains the state of <s>Brahman</s>. That which is the second <s>mātrā</s>, having <s>Viṣṇu</s> as its deity, dark in color — whoever meditates on it constantly, he attains the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. That which is the third <s>mātrā</s>, having <s>Īśāna</s> as its deity, tawny in color — whoever meditates on it constantly, he attains the state of <s>Īśāna</s>. That which is the three-and-a-half <s>mātrā</s>, having all deities, having become unmanifest, moving in space, pure, crystal-like in color — whoever meditates on it constantly, he attains the state free from affliction. This is to be worshipped — the sages speak of it through speech, [yet] there is no grasping of it. This is the path ordained northward, by which the gods go, by which the ancestors go, by which the <s>ṛṣis</s> [go] — the supreme, the ultimate refuge.

children.text: bālāgramātraṃ hṛdayasya madhye viśvaṃ devaṃ jātarūpaṃ vareṇyam /
children.translated_text: Of the measure of a hair-tip, in the center of the heart, the universal God, golden, most excellent —

children.text: tam ātmasthaṃ ye tu paśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ śāntir bhavati netareṣām //
children.translated_text: those wise ones who see Him dwelling within the self, for them there is peace, not for others.

children.text: yasmin krodhaṃ yāṃ ca tṛṣṇāṃ kṣamāṃ cākṣamāṃ hitvā hetujālasya mūlam /
children.translated_text: In whom [having abandoned] anger, desire, forbearance, and impatience — the root of the net of causes —

children.text: buddhyā saṃcitaṃ sthāpayitvā tu rudre rudram ekatvam āhuḥ //
children.translated_text: having established [all] with intellect in <s>Rudra</s>, they declare <s>Rudra</s> to be the One.

body.text: rudro hi śāśvatena vai purāṇeneṣam ūrjeṇa tapasā niyantāgnir iti bhasma vāyar iti bhasma jalam iti bhasma sthalam iti bhasma vyomam iti bhasma sarvaṃ ha vā idaṃ bhasma mana etāni cakṣūṃṣi yasmād vratam idaṃ pāśupataṃ yad bhasmanāṅgāni saṃspṛśet tasmād brahma tad etat pāśupataṃ paśupāśavimokṣaṇāya //
body.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> is indeed eternal, the ancient one; with food and vigor, through <s>tapas</s> (austerity), He is the controller. Fire is ash; wind is ash; water is ash; earth is ash; space is ash — all this indeed is ash. The mind and these eyes — since this is the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow (<s>vrata</s>), that one touches the limbs with ash — therefore, that <s>Brahman</s>, that is the <s>Pāśupata</s> [truth], for the liberation from the bonds of the bound soul (<s>paśupāśavimokṣaṇa</s>).

body.text:
yo 'gnau rudro yo 'psv antar ya oṣadhīr vīrudha āviveśa /
ya imā viśvā bhuvanāni caklape tasmai rudrāya namo 'stv agnaye /
yo rudro 'gnau yo rudro 'psv antar yo rudra oṣadhīr vīrudha āviveśa /
yo rudra imā viśvā bhuvanāni caklape tasmai rudrāya namonamaḥ /
yo rudro 'psu yo rudra oṣadhiṣu yo rudro vanaspatiṣu /
yena rudreṇa jagad ūrdhvaṃ dhāritaṃ pṛthivī dvidhā tridhā dhartā dhāritā nāgā ye 'ntarikṣe tasmai rudrāya vai namonamaḥ /
mūrdhānam asya saṃsevyāpy atharvā hṛdayaṃ ca yat /
mastiṣkād ūrdhvaṃ prerayaty avamāno 'dhiśīrṣataḥ //
body.translated_text: He who in fire is <s>Rudra</s>, who is within the waters, who has entered the herbs and plants — He who has encompassed all these worlds — to that <s>Rudra</s>, salutation, to <s>Agni</s>! He who is <s>Rudra</s> in fire, who is <s>Rudra</s> within the waters, who is <s>Rudra</s> who has entered the herbs and plants, who is <s>Rudra</s> who has encompassed all these worlds — to that <s>Rudra</s>, salutation upon salutation! He who is <s>Rudra</s> in the waters, who is <s>Rudra</s> in the herbs, who is <s>Rudra</s> in the trees — by whom, <s>Rudra</s>, the world above is upheld, the earth in two ways and three ways sustained, the <s>nāgas</s> who are in the atmosphere — to that <s>Rudra</s>, indeed, salutation upon salutation! Having attended to the head of this [<s>Atharva Veda</s>] and that which is the heart of <s>Atharvan</s> — from the brain upward He sends forth, pressing down from above the head.

body.text:
tad vā atharvaṇaḥ śiro devakośaḥ samujjhitaḥ /
tat prāṇo 'bhirakṣati śiro 'ntam atho manaḥ /
na ca divo devajanena guptā na cāntarikṣāṇi na ca bhūma imāḥ yasminn idaṃ sarvam otaprotaṃ tasmād anyaṃ na paraṃ kiṃca nāsti //
body.translated_text: That indeed is the head of the <s>Atharvan</s>, the treasure-chest of the gods, cast forth. That <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) protects the head, and also the mind. Neither guarded by the divine host from the sky, nor from the atmospheres, nor from these earths — that in which all this is woven as warp and woof — than that, there is nothing higher whatsoever.

children.text: na tasmāt pūrvaṃ na paraṃ tad asti na bhūtaṃ nota bhavyaṃ yad āsīt /
children.translated_text: Before it there is nothing, nor after it; there was nothing that was past, nor that which is yet to be.

children.text: sahasrapād ekamūrdhnā vyāptaṃ sa evedam āvarīvartti bhūtam //
children.translated_text: With a thousand feet, one-headed, all-pervading — He indeed encompasses all that has come into being.

body.text: akṣarāt saṃjāyate kālaḥ kālād vyāpaka ucyate //
body.translated_text: From the Imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>) is born; from time, the All-Pervading (<s>vyāpaka</s>) is said [to arise].

body.text:
vyāpako hi bhagavān rudro bhogāyamāno yadā śete rudras tadā saṃhāryyate prajāḥ /
ucchvasite tamo bhavati tamasa āpo 'psv aṅgulyā mathite mathitaṃ śiśire śiśiraṃ mathyamānaṃ phenaṃ bhavati phenād aṇḍaṃ bhavaty aṇḍād brahmā bhavati brahmaṇo vāyuḥ vāyor oṃkāraḥ oṃkārāt sāvitrī sāvitryā gāyatrī gāyatryā lokā bhavanti /
arcayanti tapaḥ satyaṃ madhu kṣaranti yad dhruvam /
etaddhi paramaṃ tapaḥ /
āpo jyotī raso 'mṛtaṃ brahma bhūr bhuvaḥ svar oṃ nama iti //
body.translated_text: For the Blessed <s>Rudra</s> is all-pervading. When <s>Rudra</s>, enjoying himself, lies down to sleep, then beings are withdrawn [in dissolution]. When he exhales, darkness arises. From darkness, waters [arise]. When the waters are churned with a finger, what is churned becomes cold. The cold, being churned, becomes foam. From the foam, an egg arises. From the egg, <s>Brahmā</s> arises. From <s>Brahmā</s>, wind. From wind, <s>Oṃkāra</s>. From <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [verse]. From the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter]. From the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the worlds arise. They worship — austerity, truth — they stream forth honey, that which is eternal. This indeed is the supreme austerity. Waters, light, essence, immortality, <s>Brahman</s>, <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>, <s>Oṃ</s> — homage!

body.text:
ya idam atharvaśiro brāhmaṇo 'dhīte aśrotriyaḥ śrotriyo bhavati anupanīta upanīto bhavati so 'gnipūto bhavati sa vāyupūto bhavati sa sūryapūto bhavati sa somapūto bhavati sa satyapūto bhavati sa sarvair devair jñāto bhavati sa sarvair vedair anudhyāto bhavati sa sarveṣu tīrtheṣu snāto bhavati tena sarvaiḥ kratubhir iṣṭaṃ bhavati gāyatryāḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi japtāni bhavanti itihāsapurāṇānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ śatasahasrāṇi japtāni bhavanti /
praṇavānām ayutaṃ japtaṃ bhavati /
sa cakṣuṣaḥ paṅktiṃ punāti /
ā saptamāt puruṣayugān punātīty āha bhagavān atharvaśiraḥ sakṛj japtvaiva śuciḥ sa pūtaḥ karmaṇyo bhavati /
dvitīyaṃ japtvā gaṇādhipatyam āpnoti /
tṛtīyaṃ japtvaivam evānupraviśaty oṃ satyam oṃ satyam oṃ satyam /
ity atharvavede śiraupaniṣat samāptā //
body.translated_text: The brahmin who studies this <s>Atharvaśiras</s> — if unlearned, becomes learned; if uninitiated, becomes initiated. He becomes purified by fire. He becomes purified by wind. He becomes purified by the sun. He becomes purified by the moon. He becomes purified by truth. He becomes known by all the gods. He becomes contemplated by all the <s>Vedas</s>. He becomes as one who has bathed at all sacred fords. By him it is as if sacrifice has been performed with all rituals. Sixty thousand recitations of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> are accomplished. A hundred thousand recitations of the <s>Itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and hymns to <s>Rudra</s> are accomplished. Ten thousand recitations of <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) are accomplished. He purifies a row of ten at a meal (<s>paṅkti</s>). He purifies seven generations of descendants — thus says the Blessed One. Having recited the <s>Atharvaśiras</s> once, he becomes pure, purified, and fit for ritual action. Having recited it a second time, he obtains lordship over the <s>Gaṇas</s>. Having recited it a third time, he thus enters [the supreme] — <s>Oṃ satyam, Oṃ satyam, Oṃ satyam</s>! Thus ends the <s>Śira Upaniṣad</s> (Head Upaniṣad) of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.
